newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close down but off lows.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close down but off lows.

text.p: French stocks fell on Tuesday but finished well above their session lows as reassuring U.S. economic data offset some of the nervousness triggered by a U.S. missile attack on Iraqi military targets.
Brokers said the strength of oil shares, buoyed by higher oil prices on the back of the U.S. missile raid, also helped shore up the bourse.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 5.55 points, or 0.28 percent, at 1,971.43 after coming off a low of 1,949.71. The CAC-40 September futures contract closed down four points at 1,977. Volume was a brisk 4.11 billion francs.

A report by the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management signalled flat-to-higher economic activity in August. It calmed fears of an overheating economy and helped the U.S. stockmarket recover from early lows due partly to a Wall Street Journal report that the U.S. Federal Reserve was set to raise interest rates by a half-point if the economy did not slow down.
The U.S. Conference Board said its leading indicator rose by 0.2 percent after a 0.5 percent increase in June.
* The bourse will also be closely watching French and German economic indicators due this week -- the French second quarter GDP is due tomorrow and a 0.2 percent contraction is expected.

The indicators will provide some important clues for investors, who are worried about a resurgence of industrial unrest in France and the government's efforts to meet its budget goals and the criteria for European monetary union.
The 1997 budget will be presented officially at a cabinet meeting on September 18, a government official said on Tuesday.

* Retailer Promodes closed up 0.49 percent at 1,224 francs after announcing the sale on Monday of its money-losing German unit Promohypermarkt to the Spar Handels chain. Traders said Societe Generale raised its rating on Promodes's stock to outperform from neutral.

* Carmaker Renault SA was the biggest gainer in the CAC-40 index, climbing 1.52 percent to 113.80 francs. It said it hired Carlos Ghosn, head of tyremaker Michelin's North American activities, to head its research, purchasing, vehicle and mechanical engineering and manufacturing departments. Rival PSA Peugeot Citroen closed down 1.56 percent. Michelin ended 0.42 percent higher.

* Oil stocks rose on the back of higher oil prices and expectations of strong first-half earnings due in part to the dollar's gains. Total, due to report its results on Wednesday morning, closed up 1.21 percent at 384.50 francs.
Elf-Aquitaine, whose results are due on Thursday, closed up 1.3 percent to 381.80 francs.
* Seita fell 2.5 percent to 195 francs, continuing its decline since the announcement of a tobacco price rise.
* Other companies due to report first-half results on Wednesday include Credit Local and Danone, whose results are expected after the market's close.
